name: Lunar elevation
description: The south-pole elevation model at 20 m, averaged to 30 m.
source: LOLA LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ.TIF, NASA Goddard PGDA product 90 (NASA), https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/90

name: Lunar targets
description: Seven named candidate regions for a base (30 x 30 km windows: connecting ridge, peak near Shackleton, Nobile rim 2, Malapert massif, Mons Mouton, de Gerlache, Haworth) and a 160 km polar window. The seven pooled (1,575 cells) are the default target base_regions.
source: Names and centres: USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (USGS / IAU), https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/ , and the landing-site literature listed in data/sources.csv

name: Terrain features, the same code on both bodies
description: Per cell of about 2 km (64 x 64 pixels): slope at 240 m and 570 m, roughness at 200, 400, 800 and 1,600 m, share and depth of closed depressions (pipeline/features.py).

name: Check of the estimator on the Moon
description: Our code against NASA's own lunar slope map: median absolute difference 0.042 deg at 20 m, 0.064 deg at 30 m. The elevation grid from the PDS archive against the one we use: 1.15 m robust difference.
source: LOLA slope and roughness maps, PGDA products 90 and 70 (NASA); LOLA gridded record LDEM_80S_80M in the Planetary Data System (NASA), https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/missions/lro/

name: Earth elevation
description: 2,101 one-degree tiles chosen coarse to fine (bare ground, not flat; all ice-free polar land), 1.76 million cells. A second, NASA elevation model for the 619 tiles it covers.
source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / European Commission), https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/ (read from the AWS copy); NASADEM (NASA JPL), read from OpenTopography's public mirror

name: Land-cover mask
description: A cell can be a candidate only if at least 80% is bare ground, under 5% ice and under 5% water.
source: ESA WorldCover 2021 (ESA), https://esa-worldcover.org/ ; for the NASA variant MODIS MCD12Q1 land cover (NASA) through NASA GIBS, https://gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov/

name: Score
description: Features are log- or root-transformed; the Mahalanobis distance of an Earth cell to the lunar target is turned into p_all, the share of the target's own cells that lie farther from its centre. Candidate cell: p_all >= 0.10 and the mask.

name: Sites and ranking
description: Candidate cells that touch form a site (at least 4 cells). Sites are ranked by the similarity-weighted area of their best 15 x 15 km window, the size of a lunar candidate region. Sites with the dune-field signature (cell relief over 200 m roughness below the 5th percentile of the lunar cells) are kept but ranked last.

name: Where each analogy breaks
description: Per site: climate, a satellite image, measured day and night surface temperature, soil moisture, permafrost. Per lunar region: temperature and depth to stable ice, radar, neutron counts, illumination. None of this enters the score.
source: NASA POWER (NASA), https://power.larc.nasa.gov/ ; NASA Worldview / GIBS (NASA), https://worldview.earthdata.nasa.gov/ ; LRO Diviner, Mini-RF, LEND, LAMP, LROC in the Planetary Data System (NASA), https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/missions/lro/diviner.htm ; MODIS MOD11C1 (NASA); GCOM-C SGLI and GCOM-W AMSR2, JAXA G-Portal products (JAXA), https://gportal.jaxa.jp/ ; ESA CCI Permafrost from the ESA Open Science Catalog (ESA), https://opensciencedata.esa.int/

name: Validation and review
description: Known analog sites against random circles; negative controls; laser profiles; lidar close-ups of craters; a person-readable review of the top 30; a literature check of the top sites.
source: 75 known analog sites with a source each (data/reference/known_analogs.csv); ICESat-2 ATL06 (NASA) through SlideRule, found with NASA Earthdata, https://search.earthdata.nasa.gov/ ; USGS 3DEP lidar (USGS); GUGiK terrain model (Poland)
